nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an abelian group. If $A$ is a homomorphic image of a direct product $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$ of an infinite family $(G_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite (not necessarily abelian) groups, then $A$ is a homomorphic image of the direct product $\prod_{j \in J} H_j$ of some family $(H_j)_{j \in J}$ of finite abelian groups.
nodes.title: Abelian images of products of finite groups

nodes.summary: The proposition that every abelian group $A$ that is a homomorphic image of a direct product $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$ of an infinite family $(G_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite (not necessarily abelian) groups is also a homomorphic image of the direct product $\prod_{j \in J} H_j$ of some family $(H_j)_{j \in J}$ of finite abelian groups.

nodes.summary: For an ultrafilter $U$ on $\mathbb{N}$ and a sequence $(G_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of groups, the normal subgroup of $\prod_i G_i$ generated by the sequences $(g_i)_i$ with $\{i : g_i = 1\} \in U$. These sequences already form a normal subgroup, so the kernel consists of exactly them.
nodes.title: Ultraproduct kernel

nodes.summary: For an ultrafilter $U$ on $\mathbb{N}$ and a sequence $(G_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of groups, the ultraproduct $\left(\prod_i G_i\right)/U$ is the quotient of the direct product $\prod_i G_i$ by the ultraproduct kernel, the normal subgroup of sequences $(g_i)_i$ with $\{i : g_i = 1\} \in U$.
